surfaces.part: root flare and grass tufts at base

answer.evidence: The canopy is the main volume (rows 1-31, up to 29 px wide). It is a lumpy, sphere-like mass shaded from light at the top (rows 4-13, L about 121-135) to dark at the underside (rows 25-29, L about 29-73). Width grows steadily from 3 px at row 1 to 29 px at rows 9-11 and narrows again from row 28, so it is a rounded blob rather than a flat plate. It has no front-edge line and no horizontal ellipse plane, so I report no distinct top surface. The shading reads as volume, not a flat front elevation. Below the canopy is a trunk 5-6 px wide (rows 33-41) that flares into roots and grass at rows 42-47, widening to 25 px. This is an organic form, and the usual top-surface evidence (a)-(d) does not apply cleanly.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate canopy is a compact blob in about 4 greens with soft clumps, a thin trunk, and a few grass dots at the base. Its visible tones per tile are 9, against 26 and 29 for the references, which is about a third. Its raw colour count is 28 against 427 and 567. The references have many separate leaf clusters with bright highlights, dark gaps and a trunk with roots and branches showing through the canopy. The candidate has no branch structure inside the canopy, a smooth and rounded silhouette, and little clump definition, so it reads simpler and flatter. The outline is tinted dark green with 0% neutral edge pixels, so it is not a sticker look, and there is no flat 5x5 fill. The shading and texture depth still fall clearly below the Beodeul bar.
